Compared the v4 source state machine with the live handler. The handler starts a step timer unconditionally, maps toggle from the tile state without the source open/closed/intermediate gates, stores Firestaff direction directly in DoorBit09 although source bit 09 is 1=open/0=close, always sets DoorBit12, and has no already-moving-door direction-change branch. Source also handles destroyed doors as a no-op. Full ACTUATE_DOOR parity is absent.

Compared source STEP_DOOR with both live and candidate owners. Firestaff takes direction from timer.actor, while SPX reads DoorBit09 and requires DoorBit10 to be set; active-door reversal therefore is not consumed by the current step path. SPX also advances the source timer, processes party/creature collision and damage, and manages DoorBit10/DoorBit12 through completion. Firestaff rejects occupied-door cases instead, leaving the source collision/effect path incomplete.
